title: Base flatness detected by maximal localizations of an algebra module
statement: Let $R\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and let $N$ be a $C$-module, also regarded as an $R$-module by restriction of scalars. For a maximal ideal $Q$ of $C$ (a proper ideal maximal among proper ideals), put $N_Q=(C\setminus Q)^{-1}N$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. If $N_Q$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] for every maximal ideal $Q$ of $C$, then $N$ is flat over $R$. No finiteness, injectivity, nonzero-ring, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.
